newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark ready with Albania force plan next week.
newsitem.headline: Denmark ready with Albania force plan next week.

text.p: Denmark said on Thursday it was preparing a plan for participation in a multinational military mission to lawless Albania and expected to have a contingent in place by May 10.

"We hope to finalise our deliberations soon. I hope that we will be able to present to parliament next week a proposal on Danish participation," Danish foreign minister Niels Helveg Petersen said at told a news conference.
"I cannot inform you of the details at the moment, we are still working on it and are in constant consultation with the Italians, who are leading the force," he said.
"The Danish contingent is foreseen to be in place (in Albania) around May 10," Petersen said.
There is overwhelming majority support in Denmark's parliament for Danish participation in the multinational force for Albania.

Petersen was speaking after chairing a one-day meeting of Swiss, Danish and Polish foreign ministers -- the troika of past, present and future chairmen of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).

Petersen said the first contingents of French and Spanish soldiers would arrive in Albania in mid-April but added that final details of the mandate for the Italian-led multinational force of some 6,000 troops for Albania was still not finalised.
The force will include soldiers from France, Spain, Turkey, Greece and Romania to protect the delivery of emergency food and medicine supplies to Albania.

"The details of the mandate are not finalised. I cannot explain details of the modalities for the deployment but I can only say that collecting some of the enormous amount of handguns in Albania is going to be a very important part of the force's task," he said.
In a joint statement after the meeting the troika voiced concern about friction in Belarus, where protesters and police clashed during recent opposition rallies.
They welcomed the Belarus government's acceptance of an OSCE delegation to the former Soviet Republic, which Petersen said would leave on April 15.

On Croatia, the ministers said that they were working to prepare an enhanced OSCE presence in Eastern Slavonia to ensure continued monitoring of human rights in the wake of the departure of the U.N. Transitional Administration there.
They also said they were worried about the lack of dialogue between government and opposition forces in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia on democratic reform.
